content.text:
Fixed. The leak had two listeners per `fetch()`, and only one of them was ever removed deterministically.

## Root cause

`new Request(input, { signal })` makes the request's own signal *follow* the user's signal by adding an `abort` listener to it (`lib/web/fetch/request.js:440`). That listener was only removed on abort, or when the internal `AbortController` got collected via `requestFinalizer` — i.e. on GC. `fetch()` also keeps the request object alive for the duration of the fetch (`requestObject` is passed to `fetching`). So reusing one signal across many requests piled up one listener per request until GC caught up, which is what produces `MaxListenersExceededWarning` (the existing `test/fetch/long-lived-abort-controller.js` even calls `gc()` explicitly and notes it "relies on GC").

## Changes

- `lib/web/fetch/request.js`: capture the disposer returned by `util.addAbortListener` and store a cleanup closure on the instance under a new `kSignalAbortCleanup` symbol; expose it through a `removeSignalAbortListener(request)` static, following the existing `setRequestSignal`/`getRequestState` accessor pattern (destructured, `Reflect.deleteProperty`'d, exported). Cleanup unregisters the finalizer entry and removes the listener.
- `lib/web/fetch/index.js`: keep the disposer from the step-11 `addAbortListener`, and add a `removeAbortListeners()` helper that drops both that listener and the request's follow-listener. It runs from `handleFetchDone` — the spec's process-response-end-of-body, which fires after the response body stream finishes (or immediately when there is no body, including network errors) — and also once the local abort steps have run. `handleFetchDone` moved from module scope into `fetch()` so it can close over the cleanup; the numbered spec comments are unchanged and the new code is marked undici-specific.

Because the internal request object created inside `fetch()` is never exposed to the user, dropping its follow relationship after the fetch is over isn't observable; requests the user holds (`new Request(...)`, `clone()`) are untouched. Aborting mid-stream still works — cleanup happens only after the body is done.

`lib/web/fetch/response.js` (the flagged co-change partner) needed no change: it carries only the inner response's `aborted` flag, no signal wiring.

## Verification

- New `test/fetch/abort-listener-cleanup.js`: 100 sequential fetches on one shared signal end with 0 `abort` listeners (no `gc()`); aborting after a completed read doesn't reject; an in-flight fetch still rejects with `AbortError` and shows exactly 1 listener while pending. All 3 pass.
- All of `test/fetch/*.js`: 470 pass, 0 fail (includes `long-lived-abort-controller.js`, `max-listeners.js`, `abort.js`, `abort2.js`, `issue-4627.js`, `fetch-leak.js`). `test/eventsource/*.js` + `test/cache/*.js`: 102 pass, 0 fail.

Two things I could not run: the WPT suite (`test/web-platform-tests/wpt` submodule is not checked out here) and `eslint` (the command needed approval I don't have). Nothing is committed.
